key_insight: For ICH acuity extraction from radiology reports, an open-weight Gemma-3-12B model fine-tuned on distilled real GPT-4o-labeled reports matched GPT-4o performance, while synthetic-data training did not.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals can build a private, lower-cost, on-premises text-labeling pipeline for radiology report structuring without relying on proprietary hosted models.
method: 2x2 comparison: classification head vs instruction fine-tuning
Training data: distilled real GPT-4o labels vs GPT-4o-generated synthetic reports
Evaluated across five training sizes on 100 expert-adjudicated head-CT reports
evidence_signal: The distilled instruction-tuned model achieved macro-F1 0.845 versus GPT-4o at 0.850 and outperformed the un-tuned base model by 0.178; synthetic-data models never beat the base model.
watch_item: Results come from a narrow task and dataset, so performance and deployment feasibility may not generalize to other report types, institutions, or labeling targets.
paper_title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports
